claims.text: Arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys form an ordered single-phase hexagonal state.
The ordered single-phase state undergoes a first-order magnetostructural transition.
Bulk samples exhibit a large, sharp, and highly hysteretic entropy change.
The large, sharp, and hysteretic entropy change is caused by a uniform ordered single-phase structure.
Systematically varying sputtered-film thickness will tune nanoscale interface density and grain-boundary population while nominal composition remains constant.
Film thickness controls the density of grain boundaries and short-range chemical order.
Thinner films have higher nanoscale interface density.
Higher interface density supplies additional nucleation sites for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Additional transition nucleation sites produce smoother magnetostructural transitions.
Additional transition nucleation sites reduce transition hysteresis.
Bulk forms contain fewer relevant interfaces than thinner films.
The larger surface-to-volume ratio of thin films improves heat transfer relative to bulk forms.
Increasing nanoscale interface density will reduce hysteresis width relative to bulk as-deposited samples.
Increasing nanoscale interface density will improve transition kinetics relative to bulk as-deposited samples.
Thinner films will retain a sufficiently high magnetocaloric response during low-applied-field cycles.
The predicted behavior is limited to film thicknesses that preserve mechanical integrity and the ordered hexagonal structure.

contradictions.description: The initial state labels arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons as 'as-deposited,' whereas the intervention uses as-deposited sputtered thin films and the outcome treats the bulk forms as comparison baselines. This leaves the actual initial material form ambiguous.
